newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament debates investment funds bill.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament debates investment funds bill.

text.p: The lower house of parliament on Friday began to debate a draft law on investment funds, which allows for the creation of close-ended funds in Poland.
"The bill will contribute to the development of the capital market in Poland and to more trust in savings institutions," Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz told the house presenting the draft.

Under the bill, sent to committees for further scrutiny, the Polish Securities Commission will grant permits for institutions called investment fund societies to run open-ended, specialist open-ended, closed and mixed investment funds.
The law has so far allowed only to create open-ended funds. Operations of the close-ended National Investment Funds (NFI) are regulated by a special law on mass privatisation.
Under the bill, the investment fund society would have to have a capital of at least four million zlotys to run one fund.
The close-ended funds would be allowed to issue investment certificates, securities which could be traded on the bourse.
Such funds would not redeem the certificates as the mixed funds, which could also list their certificates.
